result.title: Hilbert States for Decision-Making under Partial Observability
result.summary: Decision-making under partial observability can be fundamentally limited by information, even with known dynamics: distinct physical states can induce the same observation history while favoring different actions. We study three questions: when is full-state optimality unattainable, what information exactly preserves the best observation-based decision, and how does finite-data learning affect reliability? First, we characterize decision ambiguity through conditional action preferences. We give a zero-regret criterion, a positive lower bound for conflicting uniquely optimal actions on positive-probability regions with uniformly positive cost gaps, and an exact binary-action regret formula. This also shows why physical-state ambiguity alone need not cause decision loss. Second, for two actions and squared terminal-goal costs in the plane, we derive an exact inner-product representation of conditional expected cost differences using three conditional moment contrasts and a goal-dependent feature. This Hilbert state preserves observation-optimal actions without hidden-state reconstruction. Under nondegenerate history and goal variation, its three-dimensional form is minimal among exact bilinear cost-contrast representations. Third, we relate finite-data state errors to excess decision regret via goal-projected errors, action margins, and goal geometry. Physics-based simulations verify information-limited regret, exact action preservation, and the role of second moments. Held-out real-SAR experiments demonstrate feasible goal-conditioned decisions from masked images, while finite-data evaluations reveal goal-dependent reliability. Together, these results separate irreducible information loss, exact representation sufficiency, and learning-induced excess regret.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在部分可观测决策中刻画「决策歧义」与零遗憾条件，并在两动作、平方终端代价的平面设定下导出由三个条件矩对比构成的三维 Hilbert 状态，论证其保持观测最优动作且维数最小，再用仿真与真实 SAR 实验检验有限数据带来的额外遗憾。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「哪些信息足以保持最优决策」的最小充分状态与目标投影误差分析，可能为 LVR 中 latent 应保留何种任务必要信息、目标条件如何影响状态充分性提供概念参照；但设定属 POMDP 理论与 SAR 决策，与 VLM 推理距离较远，可供核查。
